proposed.text: A residential dwelling (180 sqm) has: lighting (2 VA/sqm), 3 small appliance circuits (1,500 VA each), 1 laundry circuit (1,500 VA), water heater (3,500 VA), air conditioner (2,200 VA), and 35 convenience outlets (180 VA each). Calculate the total connected load.
proposed.rationale: Connected load = sum of all loads at nameplate/unit values. Lighting = 180 x 2 = 360 VA. Small appliance = 3 x 1,500 = 4,500 VA. Laundry = 1,500 VA. Water heater = 3,500 VA. Air conditioner = 2,200 VA. Outlets = 35 x 180 = 6,300 VA. Total = 360 + 4,500 + 1,500 + 3,500 + 2,200 + 6,300 = 18,360 VA. The original '21,360 VA' answer inflated the outlet count; the model-generated rationale itself admitted the sum equals 18,360 VA. Source: PEC 220.12 general lighting and branch-circuit/receptacle load provisions.
